answer: Staked curation stops bulk fake identities by putting every endorsement at financial risk. A newcomer files a work history, and a grove of five unrelated curators must stake 60 credits to activate. Each stake enters a cedar log, so a curator who approved a fake loses the bond. The k-th fake needs a fresh stake and history, so 1,000 fakes risk 60,000 credits with no reuse, while an honest agent passes once. Curator rental fails because the rented curator still pays the slash, and honest curators earn fees, so each identity's voyage through vetting is its proof.
